holidays.name: National Chocolate Day
holidays.description: A day for unwrapping, melting, dunking and nibbling every kind of chocolate there is. Dark, milk, truffles and fudge all count. It lands just before Halloween, so it doubles as a convenient warm-up for candy season.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial, informal observance. It has become a fixture on the American food-holiday calendar as Halloween approaches.
holidays.funFact: Cacao was once so prized in ancient Mesoamerica that its beans were used as currency.

holidays.name: International Animation Day
holidays.description: A worldwide celebration of animated film, from hand-drawn classics to stop-motion oddities and modern computer-generated blockbusters. Fans mark the day with screenings, workshops and cartoon marathons.
holidays.origin: It was established in 2002 by ASIFA, the International Animated Film Association. It commemorates the first public commercial film screening by Émile Reynaud on October 28, 1892, at the Musée Grévin in Paris, which used his Théâtre Optique.
holidays.funFact: Reynaud's 1892 show used hand-painted strips of images projected onto a screen. That was decades before Mickey Mouse was drawn.

holidays.name: Plush Animal Lover's Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate teddy bears, stuffed bunnies and every other cuddly companion. Hug a fuzzy friend, dust off your childhood stuffed animal, or give a new plush to someone who needs one.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is popular with collectors and plush fans.
holidays.funFact: The teddy bear is named after U.S. President Theodore "Teddy" Roosevelt, following a 1902 hunting trip story.
